A1.justification: Both complete 39-page PDFs describe Discount Model Search and contain corresponding main sections and Appendices A–G. Text and visual inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, results, and presentation.

before.justification: v3 reports original DMS and baseline performance, runtime measurements, and ablation results across benchmark and image-based QDDM domains (Tables 1–2; Appendices B and D).

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and their outcomes, including performance comparisons, runtime measurements, and ablations (Tables 1–2; Appendices B and D).

M1.justification: The CMA-ES emitters, neural discount model, regression targets, empty-point training, and archive updates are unchanged (Section 5, Algorithm 1, Equation 1, and Appendix C).

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same eight Linear Projection benchmarks, Arm Repertoire, TA (MNIST), TA (F-MNIST), and LSI (Hiker) using LHQ images (Section 6; Table 1).

E2.justification: Both compare against CMA-MAE, DDS, MAP-Elites (line), and MAP-Elites on the benchmarks. DDS remains excluded from the QDDM comparisons in both versions (Table 1; Section 7.1).

E3.justification: The 10,000-iteration budget, archive configurations, sample sizes, objective normalization, and QD Score/Coverage metrics remain unchanged (Sections 6–7; Appendices C and E). Figure 3 changes axis presentation without changing the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Both retain the distortion experiment, archive and discount-model visualizations, and ablations of archive learning rate, empty points, and restart rules (Figure 1; Appendices B and D). No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report 20 benchmark trials and 5 QDDM trials, means and standard errors, and the same Welch ANOVA and Games-Howell testing procedures (Section 7.1; Appendix B).

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, DMS retains a QD Score of 7,406.01 and Coverage of 95.97% on 20D LP (Sphere) in Table 1 and Figure 3. The revised Figure 3 rescales the same plotted results.

T1.justification: The QD formulation, discount-target equation, manifold assumption, and mathematical domain definitions are unchanged (Sections 2, 5, and 6.2; Appendix E). No mathematical reasoning or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about continuous discount models improving exploration, DMS outperforming existing algorithms, and QDDM enabling diversity specification through datasets.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including discount-model noise, computational overhead, dataset availability, nearest-neighbor scalability, and difficulties applying differentiable QD to QDDM (Sections 7.1 and 8; Appendices A, C, and G).

D1.justification: Code-access instructions, hyperparameters, model architecture and training details, data processing, hardware, and resource disclosures match (Section 10; Appendices C, E, and F).

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationships to CMA-MAE, DDS, surrogate models, learned measures, and feedback-based QD methods (Section 3; Appendix A).

P1.justification: v5 adds numbered author-affiliation mappings and Archimedes AI as a second affiliation for Stefanos Nikolaidis, and removes the separate Los Angeles location line. Scientific wording and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 standardizes the 20D and 50D LP (Sphere) panels to QD Score ticks of 0, 4,000, and 8,000 and Coverage ticks of 0%, 50%, and 100%, replacing differing scales and fractional labels. The affiliation edit also causes limited text reflow across pages 1–6.

improvement.justification: Figure 3's consistent scales and percentage labels make performance across Sphere benchmark dimensionalities easier to compare. This provides a modest presentation benefit, while the scientific evidence, conclusions, and limitations remain unchanged.
